provenance: Existing-data readout ONLY. Derived from already-committed per-run scorer summaries (prescription/lawv1/e500_scores/e500s_*_summary.json). No new training, no new inference. The paired quantity is computed by the frozen scorer itself (prescription/lawv1_score.py summarize(): paired_family = mean over families of [original.acc_exact AND condition.acc_exact], same family_id = same underlying item).

definition.paired_family: fraction of evaluation families with BOTH original and perturbed condition correct (acc_exact), same-family pairing
definition.conditional_fragility: P(perturbed failure | original correct) = (original.acc_exact - paired_family) / original.acc_exact

scope_note: Formal-scale support exists for the DISTRACTOR axis (n=529 families, all placebo arms and base). Paraphrase pairing exists only on the auxiliary 50-family frozen subset (base paired_family .82, n=50) and is auxiliary/directional, not formal evidence. The insufficient-information branch has a related committed joint (paired_answerability = P(original correct AND correct abstention)) reported separately.

auxiliary_paraphrase_base.note: auxiliary frozen subset; original accuracy restricted to these 50 families not stored in summary, so a clean conditional is not derivable — directional only

insufficient_branch_base.note: P(original correct AND correct abstention) — competence and correct abstention rarely co-occur at base

allowed_wording: About one in ten originally-correct families fails when a single distractor is inserted (placebo mean .095, range .082-.107 across 9 arms; base .119): same-item fragility, measured by same-family pairing at formal scale.
forbidden_wording: Do not extend the same-item fragility claim to paraphrase at formal scale (auxiliary 50-family subset only); do not present paired_answerability as a fragility conditional.
